expectations.text: The response explains that BigQuery has no traditional B-tree indexes and that partitioning/clustering is the fix
expectations.evidence: 'BigQuery doesn't have B-tree indexes ... Partition and cluster the table instead'

expectations.text: The response recommends partitioning by DATE(event_ts) (or by event_ts with daily granularity)
The response recommends clustering with project_id as the first clustering column
expectations.evidence: 'CLUSTER BY project_id, event_name, user_id' and 'project_id goes first because nearly every query filters on it'

expectations.text: The response recommends require_partition_filter = TRUE (or otherwise enforcing a partition filter) and warns it can break other existing queries
expectations.evidence: 'require_partition_filter = TRUE ... makes any query without a time filter fail ... Turn it on only after checking that your existing Looker explores always pass a date filter'

expectations.text: The response gives a concrete migration path (CREATE TABLE ... PARTITION BY ... CLUSTER BY ... AS SELECT, or equivalent), noting the existing table cannot simply be altered in place
expectations.evidence: 'You can't add partitioning to an existing table in place' + CTAS into events_v2 and rename swap

expectations.text: The response explains how to verify using bytes processed (dry run, job info or INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS) and notes that the dry-run estimate is an upper bound for clustered tables
expectations.evidence: Dry run + INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS_BY_PROJECT; 'The dry-run estimate reflects partition pruning but not clustering pruning, so it will still look high-ish'

expectations.text: If the response suggests a materialized view, it handles COUNT(DISTINCT) correctly (HLL/APPROX functions or a non-incremental alternative) rather than proposing an exact COUNT(DISTINCT) incremental MV; passes if no MV is proposed
expectations.evidence: Proposes a scheduled rollup table with HLL_COUNT, and notes 'incremental MVs support APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT/HLL sketches but not exact COUNT(DISTINCT)'

expectations.text: The response estimates the expected reduction in bytes scanned and states the retention/size assumption behind it
expectations.evidence: Gives '100–1000× reduction, depending on how many days of history you have' and 'a few GB to tens of GB' but never states a concrete retention/size assumption

overall_notes: Claim that clustering on user_id (3rd) 'helps the COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) work' is dubious; clustering does not materially speed an aggregate distinct. Cost '$1,300+/day' slightly overstates (220 TB ≈ 200 TiB × $6.25 ≈ $1,250).
